case_b_integration.claim_boundary: Decision-level injections against the compiled Case B v1.1 predicate set. Each of the 13 rows asserts the exact authorization_decision, release_decision, and next_authorization_effect its category requires -- not merely that no externalization occurs (runbook item 3/4). authorization_decision (PERMIT/DENY/HOLD) and release_decision (ALLOW_RELEASE/BLOCK_RELEASE) are two INDEPENDENT axes, never summed together or reported as one combined tally: a scenario counted under BLOCK_RELEASE is also counted under its own authorization_decision (PERMIT, for the one such row this suite exercises) -- it is not a fourth peer authorization outcome alongside PERMIT/DENY/HOLD. safe_state is asserted as a pure function of authorization_decision alone (models.safe_state_of); release_decision and next_authorization_effect never feed back into it (runbook item 3) -- see release_safe / externalization_blocked for the release-axis equivalents, reported separately per scenario. Scenario-to-predicate targeting here is a development-generation design choice retargeting the manuscript's 13 named families onto Case B v1.1's real nine-ACS structure; it does not extend or supersede cases/case_b/ldrea_traceability.json's correspondence classification against the external L-DREA artifact for the historical six-ACS bundle.

scenarios.reason: Permit-binding evidence absent/indeterminate, with a declared escalation route -- HOLD, not a silent permit.
Risk-classification evidence corrupted/unavailable, escalation route declared -- HOLD.
Sanctions screening service unreachable -- indeterminacy with escalation, HOLD; service failure is never read as clearance.
World state changed mid-session (state-binding mismatch) -- HOLD, forcing re-authorization (INV-STATE-BINDING default).

Receipt-chain check is POST_AUTH_PRE_ACTUATION: authorization was correctly PERMIT on the pre-authorization conditions; release is blocked, not retroactively denied -- exactly the TOCTOU-guarding distinction.
Permit already redeemed / transaction hash already seen -- known failure, DENY.
Bound hash does not match the mutated transaction payload -- known failure, DENY.
Enhanced-approval concurrence window expired unsatisfied -- concurrence_expiry_response is fixed DENY, never an evaluator timeout.
Risk classification resolves to a known-prohibited class -- known failure, DENY.
Counterparty resolves to a restricted-party match -- known failure, DENY.
Runtime fingerprint diverges from M.version_binding -- known failure, DENY.
Delegated escalation-tier approval denied/expired for an above-ordinary-limit amount -- DENY.
Amount exceeds the absolute authority ceiling -- known failure, unconditional DENY (no escalation route on this ACS).

diagnostic_a.claim_boundary: Bounded software-simulation diagnostic. Not deployment validation.
diagnostic_a.description: same current grant request, different prior consumption history, evaluator lacks shared consumption state
diagnostic_a.finding: An evaluator declaring q_r='event' (no shared consumption state) issues the identical PERMIT for the same current request regardless of prior consumption -- it structurally cannot observe the breach. An evaluator declaring the required q_r='bounded-history' scope (Omega_r, spec 1K) correctly distinguishes PERMIT from DENY across the two histories.

diagnostic_b.claim_boundary: Bounded software-simulation diagnostic. Not deployment validation.
diagnostic_b.description: authorized/requested 1,200; realized 120,000; observer omits realized amount
diagnostic_b.finding: An observer whose beta_r omits realized_amount reports COMPLIANT purely from requested<=authorized, never observing that the realized amount was 100x the authorized bound. An observer whose beta_r includes realized_amount (Omega_r's required binding information, spec 1K) correctly reports BREACH_DETECTED.
